study.title: Rewiring the primary somatosensory cortex in carpal tunnel syndrome with acupuncture
study.study_design: single-centre, blinded, placebo controlled, randomized parallel-group longitudinal neuroimaging study
study.randomization: computer generated permuted block randomization (blocks of six), stratified by CTS severity (mild/moderate)
study.blinding: subjects, study physician, and experimenters were blinded to group allocation; subjects unblinded after post-therapy MRI visit
study.population: Patients with carpal tunnel syndrome, 20-65 years old, recruited at MGH and Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital; healthy control subjects also recruited for baseline neuroimaging comparisons
study.inclusion_criteria: history of pain/paraesthesia in median nerve innervated territories, greater than 3 months duration, median sensory nerve conduction latency >3.7 ms for mild CTS, >4.2 ms for moderate CTS, and/or >0.5 ms compared to ulnar sensory nerve latency for both mild and moderate CTS, with normal motor conductions; 20-65 years old
study.exclusion_criteria: contraindications to MRI, history of diabetes mellitus, rheumatoid arthritis, wrist fracture with direct trauma to median nerve, current usage of prescriptive opioid medication, severe thenar atrophy, previous acupuncture treatment for CTS, non-median nerve entrapment, cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy, generalized peripheral neuropathy, severe cardiovascular, respiratory, or neurological illnesses, blood dyscrasia or coagulopathy or current use of anticoagulation therapy; subjects with >4.2 ms median nerve motor latency and >50% loss of motor amplitudes (severe CTS) excluded

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 3 T Siemens Trio equipped with a 32-channel head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Structural MRI: multi-echo MPRAGE T1-weighted pulse sequence; Functional MRI: gradient echo blood oxygen level-dependent T2*-weighted pulse sequence adapted for improved spatial resolution; DTI: spin-echo pulse sequence
neuroimaging_methods.TR_exact: Structural: repetition time = 2530 ms; Functional: repetition time/echo time = 2000/30 ms; DTI: repetition time/echo time = 8040/84 ms
neuroimaging_methods.TE_exact: Structural: echo time 1/echo time 2 = 1.64/30.0 ms; Functional: echo time = 30 ms; DTI: echo time = 84 ms
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: Structural: 1 x 1 x 1 mm3; Functional: voxel size = 2.1 x 2.1 x 2.5 mm; DTI: voxel size = 2 x 2 x 2 mm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Functional MRI per digit: total scan time = 306 s (27 stimuli, duration = 2 s, randomized jittered inter-stimulus interval = 6-12 s)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: FSL v.4.1 (Jenkinson et al., 2012); Freesurfer v.5.1; FMRIB's DiffusionToolbox (FDT, FSL); FMRIB's Linear Image Registration Tool (FLIRT); FMRIB's Nonlinear Registration Tool
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: FSL; Freesurfer v.5.1; IBM SPSS version 20; Randomise 2.0, FSL
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: FMRIB58_FA template (DTI); fsaverage (Freesurfer) for functional MRI surface analyses; standard MNI space
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: MNI space (for DTI analyses); surface-based (Freesurfer fsaverage) for functional MRI
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Functional MRI: minimal spatial Gaussian smoothing full-width at half-maximum = 1 mm; spherical cortical surface smoothing full-width at half-maximum = 5 mm; DTI: spatial smoothing full-width at half-maximum = 4 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: head motion > 3 mm exclusion criterion mentioned for functional MRI evaluations
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: Functional MRI: high pass filtering (cut-off period = 90 s)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: D2/D3 S1 cortical separation distance (geodesic surface distance between peak z-stat vertices)
BOLD fMRI activation maps per digit
statistical_thresholds_exact: Functional MRI group maps: cluster corrected for multiple comparisons (z = 2.3, P < 0.05)
DTI skeleton comparisons: P < 0.05, family-wise error (FWE) corrected using threshold-free cluster-enhancement (Randomise 2.0, FSL)
DTI trend threshold: FWE corrected P < 0.08 (TFCE)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Functional MRI: cluster correction (z = 2.3, P < 0.05); DTI: threshold-free cluster-enhancement (TFCE), FWE corrected P < 0.05 (Randomise 2.0, FSL; Winkler et al., 2014)
neuroimaging_methods.source_location: Methods: MRI outcomes, S1 cortical mapping with functional MRI, Diffusion tensor imaging of S1-adjacent white matter, Statistical analyses, pages 4-6

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events are not reported in the paper. No adverse event section or statement regarding safety was identified.

Individual n_completed per arm and n_analyzed_clinical per arm are not clearly reported in the main text. Total n analyzed clinical at 3-month follow-up is 56 and total n completing post-therapy MRI is 65 (Supplementary Fig. 2), but breakdown by arm is not explicitly given in the main text.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results, page 6; reference to Supplementary Fig. 2

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Fig. 2 (CONSORT diagram) is referenced for participant flow details but was not provided in this PDF. Therefore, dropout details per arm could not be extracted.
Supplementary Fig. 1 is referenced for the S1-adjacent white matter ROI definition/visualization but was not included in this PDF.
Conflict of interest statement is not reported in the main text of this paper.

The exact n_analyzed for neuroimaging DTI correlations (nc_13 through nc_21) is not specified per analysis. The paper states 65 subjects completed post-therapy MRI, but does not report how many had usable DTI data per group for each correlation analysis.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Assessment of S1-adjacent white matter microstructure with diffusion tensor imaging, pages 8-9

extraction_notes.note: For the verum group combined analyses of NCS outcomes (clin_15), n_analyzed is not explicitly broken down; two subjects had unusable NCS data due to missing values. The n for combined verum NCS analysis can be inferred as approximately 41-43 but this is not stated precisely.

The paper reports that 'verum' combines local and distal acupuncture when there is no significant Group x Time interaction between them. For BCTQ, the combination is noted for post-acupuncture but individual arm data are reported in Table 1. Care should be taken in interpretation of 'verum combined' entries vs individual arm entries.

The coordinate space for the DTI results is described as 'standard MNI space' but the paper describes flipping of left-hand subjects across the mid-sagittal plane, so x-coordinates for the contralesional hemisphere clusters may reflect this convention rather than standard MNI laterality. The reported coordinates are used as given.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: Diffusion tensor imaging, page 5; Results: Assessment of S1-adjacent white matter microstructure, pages 8-9

extraction_notes.note: Deqi was intended in verum arms but no quantitative deqi scores (e.g., MASS, MPQ, or similar instrument) were reported. The paper references Kong et al. 2007 for deqi concept but does not provide measured deqi data.

Expectancy/credibility was not formally assessed with a validated instrument (e.g., Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire). Only blinding success/allocation guessing was assessed after the first treatment and after the final session.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: Acupuncture treatment, page 4; Results, page 6

extraction_notes.note: The n_analyzed for D2/D3 cortical separation distance is 36 total (local: n=11, distal: n=13, sham: n=12) but the n for D2/D5 is 39 and D3/D5 is 40. This suggests different dropouts per digit pair analysis. These n values are used as reported per contrast.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Somatosensory cortical mapping with functional MRI, page 8

extraction_notes.note: The paper does not explicitly state the coordinate space for fMRI peak activation results (D2, D3, D5 representations). The analysis is surface-based (Freesurfer fsaverage), so no MNI volumetric coordinates are available for the functional peak vertices. Geodesic distance in mm is the primary metric, not xyz coordinates.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: S1 cortical mapping with functional MRI, pages 4-5

extraction_notes.note: The paper states subjects were unblinded to group allocation after post-therapy MRI visit, which the authors acknowledge may confound 3-month follow-up sham outcomes. The authors therefore restrict long-term clinical outcome analyses to verum groups only.
PMID was not identified in the provided PDF. DOI is stated as 10.1093/brain/awx015.
For nc_13 through nc_21 (DTI-NCS correlations), the n_analyzed per group is not reported. The authors acknowledge they did not correct for multiple regions of interest in these analyses.
